observation.visible_scene: A grassy outdoor enclosure. A male lion with a thick dark mane is seen from a rear-three-quarter angle, its head oriented left toward a framed mirror standing on the left edge of the frame. The mirror shows the lion's own face as a reflection (not a second animal). The lion's hindquarters, tail with a dark terminal tuft, and rear legs occupy the center-right; blurred tree trunks and green grass form the background.
visible_changes: The lion's head and mane gradually lower toward the mirror across the excerpt: the reflection's face moves from the upper part of the mirror down toward the lower part, and the visible mane on the left descends correspondingly, indicating an ongoing bowing/nuzzling motion rather than a single step.

The tail tuft changes position over time: it begins relatively raised and curved to the right in the early frames, then hangs lower with the tuft near the ground in the middle frames, and sways again near the end, showing continuous tail movement.
The lion's torso and rear legs remain standing in roughly the same location relative to the frame throughout; the body does not walk or turn, only the head and tail shift.
The mirror's white frame and the background tree trunks stay at consistent positions, so the apparent motion is from the lion, not from camera panning.
The reflection tracks the lion's head movement, confirming the left-side face is a mirror image of the same lion.
outside_clip_unknowns: What motivated the lion to lower its head, and whether it makes contact with the mirror surface, is not shown.
The beginning and end of the head-lowering and tail-swaying behavior lie outside this cropped segment.
The lion's front legs and full face are obscured by its mane and the mirror frame, so their exact posture is unknown.
uncertain_details: Whether there is any slight camera drift is hard to confirm; the background is stable enough that the dominant motion is attributed to the lion.
The precise nature of the tail motion (sway vs. step-driven shift) cannot be separated cleanly from the body posture.
